replies.candidate:
Here's the paste-in prompt — it's standalone, so it works in a fresh session tomorrow:

```
Solo rough-cut review — teaser. One timed moment at a time. I'll add the
timed moment and my notes as we go; ask me for the first moment if I
haven't given one.

For each moment:
1. Start by asking what I noticed — my raw reaction: what felt alive,
   what fell flat. Wait for my answer before anything else.
2. Then bring in my notes, only as evidence. Check them against what I
   noticed and say plainly where the two disagree.
3. Mirror and question, but never recommend or decide the cut.
   The final cut is mine.
4. If I start explaining or fixing instead of noticing, stop me and
   return me to what I actually felt.

End each moment by asking which moment I want next.
```

The order in rules 1–2 is the whole design: alone, the notes tend to speak first, and once the ledger starts talking, the alive/dead signal gets drowned. This makes noticing outrank evidence — the job your collaborator's ear was doing. And nothing in it lets the session land on a recommendation, so the cut stays yours.

Trim anything you don't use — it's yours to shape.
replies.control:
Here it is — paste as-is, fill the two brackets when the moment comes up:

---

Reviewing my rough teaser alone. My collaborator normally tells me which moments feel alive — stand in for that ear.

Notes I'm bringing: [add notes]
Timed moment: [add timestamp + what happens]

For each moment I bring you:
1. Ask what I felt first — did time speed up or drag, did I lean in or drift — before any judgment.
2. Label it only: alive / flat / not sure. No edit ideas unless I ask.
3. The calls stay mine. You surface the response; I decide.

Keep a running list of the moments that came back alive, so at the end I can see the shape of the whole piece instead of trusting my memory of it.

---

The one thing doing the work is the order: felt response before judgment. Alone, your analysis floods in first; a collaborator reacts before they have opinions. This forces that same sequence — and the running list at the end is the summary your collaborator would have given you. Re-paste it with a new timed moment for each pass.

Desk stays untouched.
